subject: Temporary dedicated capacity for BrightForge pilot — sprint surge request
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary dedicated capacity for BrightForge pilot — request

Team —

BrightForge (Ethan Cole, cc'd below) has signed a short pilot agreement for their e-commerce recommender and is asking for a short-lived dedicated pool to avoid noisy-neighbor regressions during the live pilot. High-level ask:

- Carve ~4 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west (prefer us-west-2)
- Pilot window: 2 weeks, target start ~2028-07-10 (can shift by a few days)
- Autoscale: allow burst to 8 nodes for short windows (they expect spikes)
- Goal: consistent latency under 180ms p50 for inference flows to mirror prod behavior

I've attached the pilot requirements workbook with traffic estimates (brightforge_pilot_requirements.xlsx). Can infra confirm feasibility and a quick ops/approval path? If we need a formal exception packet I can draft and route.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary dedicated capacity for BrightForge pilot — request

Laura —

Quick questions to scope the carve:
- Which model variant exactly (weights size / quantization)?
- Expected sustained qps and peak qps, plus avg tokens per response (p90)?
- Any KV cache/long context use that would require larger memory footprints?
- Are you expecting persistent volumes or ephemeral instances?

If you can drop those numbers I can run a quick sizing and check conflicts with other pilots. From first glance 4 GPUs for two weeks is plausible but the autoscale bursts need policy sign-off (we have to ensure it won't impact scheduled enterprise pilots).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Capacity & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightforge.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@brightforge.com
Date: 2028-07-02T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary dedicated capacity for BrightForge pilot — request

Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turn. Details below:
- Model: Llama-3-70B quantized (8-bit Q4_K_M) — runtime footprint ~32GB per replica
- Expected sustained qps: 120 qps; expected peak qps: 450 qps (10–15 minute bursts)
- Avg response size: ~350 tokens (p90 ~900 tokens)
- KV cache: minimal for the pilot (stateless inference outside the session)
- Storage: ephemeral; no persistent volumes required
- Pilot flexibility: prefer start week of 2028-07-10 but can shift to 2028-07-17 if that helps capacity

We can provide a short MOU and PO if needed. Happy to hop on a 15-minute handoff call to align.

— Ethan Cole
Head of Platform, BrightForge
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-02T11:20:00-07:00

Kimberly — forwarding BrightForge's answers. Please prepare an exception request packet (pilot_autoscale_exception_request.pdf) and the short MOU (pilot_commitment_mou.docx) so we can get procurement signoff. Specific asks:

- Proposed carve: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved in us-west-2
- Autoscale override: allow burst to 8 nodes for up to two 48-hour windows during pilot
- Cost estimate for the two-week window and note on billing treatment (charged to BrightForge vs internal pilot credit)
- Ops runbook: preflight checklist, rollback criteria, contact oncall

Date: 2028-07-02T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary dedicated capacity for BrightForge pilot — request

Laura / Marcus / Aditya —

I've drafted the exception packet and attached the requested PDF (pilot_autoscale_exception_request.pdf). Summary / proposal:

- Allocation: 4 GPU equivalents reserved in us-west-2 for 2028-07-10 -> 2028-07-24 (flex +/- 7 days)
- Autoscale override: allow burst to 8 nodes for two discrete 48-hour windows. Any burst beyond those windows will be fenced and require manual ops approval.
- Guardrails: automated fallback to 50% of allocated pool if cluster health degrades, automated alerts to oncall + product.
- Cost: preliminary estimate attached (included in packet). Chargeback proposed: BrightForge pays for reserved allocation + billed burst usage; we can discuss crediting up to 20% as part of pilot credit.

Flags: this will consume buffer that ops currently holds for enterprise pilots on 2028-07-11 and 2028-07-18 — if they both materialize we will need to move one. Recommend we confirm BrightForge can shift start by a week if needed.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm no hard conflicts in your schedule? Aditya, please confirm product acceptance / go-ahead for the guardrails above. If we get yes from both I will route procurement and schedule the carve.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference

- Add a final cost line item to the MOU showing burst billing; ops to send the final estimate to BrightForge for PO.
